name: Scala
summary: Statically typed language from EPFL that fuses object-oriented and functional programming on the JVM (also JavaScript via Scala.js and native code via Scala Native). Scala 3 (the Dotty compiler) adds enums, givens/using clauses, union and intersection types, inline/macros metaprogramming and optional-braces syntax, with the DOT calculus as its formal foundation.

level_notes.0: scala/scala3 holds the Scala 3 compiler (dotc), TASTy tooling and the Scala 3 library; scala/scala holds the Scala 2.13 compiler (nsc) and the 2.13 standard library that Scala 3 still uses. Scala.js and Scala Native are alternative back ends with their own IRs.
level_notes.1: No external standard. The Scala Language Specification exists for 2.13 and, partially updated, for 3.4; for Scala 3 features the official 'Scala 3 Reference' is in practice the authoritative text, and the compiler is the final arbiter. Changes go through the Scala Improvement Process (SIPs). The DOT calculus papers give a machine-checked core.
level_notes.2: docs.scala-lang.org hosts the official Scala 3 Book and the older Tour of Scala; 'Programming in Scala' (1st ed.) is free online.
